seo_description: Allen kids' Christmas: Allen Rotary Christmas Parade, Santa Paws at the Allen Depot, Pictures with the Reinsteer, Kringle's Corner and a Nutcracker.
lede: The story of Christmas in Allen starts with a railroad town founded in 1870 and an Allen Christmas Parade that downtown businessman Don Rodenbaugh dreamed up in 1970, and today it runs from the historic Allen Train Depot to a live longhorn reinsteer under the downtown lights. Allen's 2026 season counts 10 events, with the Allen Rotary Christmas Parade on Sunday, December 6.
sections: A railroad town named for Ebenezer Allen

Allen was established in 1870 by a purchasing agent for the Houston and Texas Central Railway, on land in southwestern Collin County eight miles southwest of McKinney. In 1872 it was named for Ebenezer Allen, a former attorney general of Texas and a promoter of the railroad, and the H&TC built through town the same year. In 1908 the Texas Traction Company built an electric railway through Allen, and interurban service ended in 1948. The town had about 350 people by 1884 and 550 in 1915, then grew to 1,940 in 1970, 43,554 in 2000 and 104,627 in 2020.

The Allen Christmas Parade developed in the mind of downtown businessman Don Rodenbaugh in 1970 and is now presented by the Allen Rotary Club. Allen's local history blog says the first parade, created as a downtown promotion, had 52 entries and 125 horses. The Allen Heritage Guild rode in it for six years, and its 2015 float used a Polar Express theme built on Allen's railroad history, with a constructed locomotive. In 2026 the Allen Rotary Christmas Parade rolls on Sunday, December 6, at 2 pm. The theme, Hometown Christmas, celebrates Allen's 150th anniversary, and watching is free.
The depot, Heritage Village and a reinsteer

Allen's railroad past shows up in its December. The City of Allen holds Santa Paws at the historic Allen Train Depot, 100 East Main Street, on Thursday, December 10, from 5:30 to 7:30 pm, where families bring leashed dogs for a photo with Santa. On Tuesday, December 15, from 6 to 8 pm, kids can pose with a live longhorn steer called the reinsteer under the downtown holiday lights. On Thursday, December 17, from 5 to 8 pm, live reindeer visit the Allen Heritage Village Barn, 450 St. Mary Drive, a collection of historic buildings near downtown. All three are free.
trains: Allen began as a Houston and Texas Central Railway town in 1870 and had an electric interurban line from 1908 to 1948, and the old Allen Train Depot at 100 East Main Street is now a city holiday venue. The DART light rail system serves Richardson and Plano, with the Red Line ending at Parker Road Station in Plano, a short drive south. Nearby train attractions include the Interurban Railway Museum in Plano, the McKinney Avenue M-Line Trolley in Dallas and the Museum of the American Railroad in Frisco.

faq: How did Allen get its name?

Allen was named in 1872 for Ebenezer Allen, a former attorney general of Texas and a promoter of the Houston and Texas Central Railway. The town was established in 1870 by a railway purchasing agent in southwestern Collin County, and the railway built through the town in 1872, according to the Handbook of Texas.
When did the Allen Christmas Parade start?

The parade began in 1970, an idea from downtown businessman Don Rodenbaugh, according to the Allen Heritage Guild. Allen's local history blog says the first one had 52 entries and 125 horses. Today the Allen Rotary Club presents it, and in 2026 it is on Sunday, December 6, at 2 pm, free to watch.
Where can kids meet Santa for free in Allen?

Frost Bank Allen East, 498 E Stacy Road, hosts Cookies with Santa on December 2 from 4:30 to 6:30 pm, free. The North Pole at Joe Farmer Recreation Center, 1201 E Bethany Drive, is on December 12 from 9:30 am to 2:30 pm, free to attend. Santa Paws at the Allen Depot is December 10, free.
Did a train ever run through Allen?

Yes. The Houston and Texas Central Railway built through Allen in 1872, and in 1908 the Texas Traction Company built an electric railway through town. Interurban service ended in 1948. The Allen Train Depot, at 100 East Main Street, still stands and hosts the city's Santa Paws event each December.
What is the reinsteer in Allen?

The reinsteer is a live longhorn steer that visits downtown Allen for holiday photos. In 2026 families can take pictures with it on Tuesday, December 15, from 6 to 8 pm, among the downtown lights. The City of Allen lists it as free with no registration, and says it is the only night this season.
Are there free Christmas crafts in Allen?

Yes. Kringle's Corner offers free holiday crafts every Tuesday through Friday from December 1 to 24, 2026, from 11 am to 2 pm, at the Blue House Too Art Space and Gallery, 980 Watters Creek Boulevard. The Watters Creek events page lists it as free, and the midday hours suit preschoolers and winter break.
